newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative MP defects to Referendum Party.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative MP defects to Referendum Party.

text.p: Britain's small Referendum Party, which is campaigning for a plebiscite on closer integration with the European Union, said on Saturday that a Conservative member of parliament had defected to its ranks.

The Referendum Party said Sir George Gardiner had resigned from the ruling Conservatives and would sit in the parliament as a Referendum Party MP until national elections expected to be held on May 1 when he would represent the party as a candidate.

Gardiner, who has fallen out with his local Conservative Party association for criticising Prime Minister John Major, is the first Conservative MP to join the Referendum Party and the new party's first MP.
The anti-European Referendum Party was formed a year ago by millionaire businessman Sir James Goldsmith with the sole aim of securing a referendum over Britain's future in the European Union.

It is running a full-scale election campaign and political analysts say it could have a serious effect on the election fortunes of the Conservatives, who are more than 20 points behind the main opposition Labour Party in the opinion polls.
Gardiner's defection will put Major's government in a minority of two in the House of Commons (lower house of parliament. Goldsmith said Gardiner's decision "showed country must come before party".
